subject: [Customer] Evopay: sudden throughput & 5xx spike — coordinated response
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@evopay.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-10T22:03:00Z
Subject: Intermittent 5xx and high tail latency — urgent

Mina —

We started seeing a sustained rise in 5xx errors and 99th percentile latency on our payment-confirmation route around 21:40 PT. Throughput for that route jumped ~2.6x and a number of user transactions timed out. Our SREs captured traces and a small set of customer reports (attached).

Key impact: some confirmation calls are failing end-to-end (users see "payment pending") and batch retries are increasing downstream load. We are on a tight release window this morning and need immediate assistance. Can your team open an incident and let us know mitigations and expected ETA to back to normal?

Attaching: evopay-traces-20271010.log

— Marta
Marta Ruiz

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-10-10T22:28:00Z
Subject: Re: FWD: Intermittent 5xx and high tail latency — urgent

On Sun, Oct 10, 2027 at 22:20 Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding an urgent customer report from Evopay.

I'm on it. Initial read: this looks like a traffic pattern shift exposing a cache-miss storm combined with longer kv-cache fill times on the larger-sequence model. Immediate mitigations I recommend (30–90m):

1) Route Evopay's production traffic to a smaller model variant (latency-optimized) as a short-term fallback. That will reduce per-token latency and avoid large KV fills.
2) Increase Dedicated burst capacity for that pool (we have available nodes in us-west-2) — I'll request +2 workers now.
3) Apply a temporary token-limit throttle on non-critical calls (batch/analytics) from Evopay to preserve headroom.
4) Enable prefix/KV aggressive caching for confirmed-session flows for this customer.
5) If the above doesn't restore, enable a canary version with reduced max-seq and a reduced sampling ratio and monitor error rate.

I've attached a short mitigation checklist. I'll coordinate with infra to provision nodes and with SRE to open the canary. Monica — can you run a quick canary and report 15m metrics? Sean — please prepare the external status note for Marta (short, clear ETA).

Attaching: mitigation-checklist.pdf

—Karthik
VP, Serving Runtime
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: mina.haddad@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-11T01:12:00Z
Subject: Re: FWD: Intermittent 5xx and high tail latency — urgent (canary update)

On Sun, Oct 10, 2027 at 22:28 Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I've attached a short mitigation checklist. I'll coordinate with infra to provision nodes and with SRE to open the canary. Monica — can you run a quick canary and report 15m metrics?

Canary executed at 00:30 PT against the reduced-seq model variant (sampling 10%). Early results (first 30m):
- 99th latency dropped from ~1.8s to ~450ms for the sampled requests.
- 5xx rate on the route dropped from 6.2% -> 0.9% in the canary slice.
- Overall cluster CPU on the backup pool increased by ~12% (within expected burst headroom).

Conclusion: the smaller model + caching mitigations appear to address the tail. Next step: expand canary to 40% and monitor 30m before full reroute.

Attaching: canary-metrics-20271011.csv

Monica Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@evopay.com>, Evopay Ops <ops@evopay.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, cio@evopay.com
Date: 2027-10-11T04:58:00Z
Subject: Evopay incident update — current status and next steps

Marta — thank you for raising this quickly and for the traces. Short update from the bridge and next steps (TL;DR below).

TL;DR: We observed a traffic pattern shift that caused cache-miss amplification on the large-sequence model. We ran a targeted mitigation (short-term reroute to latency-optimized variant + aggressive KV/prefix caching) and executed a controlled canary. Canary metrics show 99th latency and 5xx rate for the sampled traffic returned to acceptable levels. We are expanding the canary and will do a full reroute when metrics are stable.

What we did (summary):
- Opened incident (RED-8872) at 22:10 PT and assembled a cross-functional bridge (SRE, Serving, Infra, CS).
- Applied temporary routing to latency-optimized model and enabled aggressive KV caching for confirmed-session flows.
- Provisioned +2 burst workers in us-west-2 to handle the short-term load spike.
- Ran a canary (10% -> 40%) with monitoring on 99th latency, 5xx rate, and customer-perceived errors.

Current status (04:58 PT):
- Canary (40%) is stable for 30m: 5xx rate in canary slice 0.8% vs baseline 5.9% prior to mitigation.
- End-to-end confirmation failures reduced by ~85% for sampled customers.
- Infrastructure headroom remains (no additional preemption required).

Planned next steps (timeline):
- 05:30 PT: Expand canary to 80% if metrics remain stable (monitoring window 30m).
- 06:15 PT: Full reroute to the latency-optimized model and keep burst workers for 6 hours; rollback plan ready if error rate rises.
- 08:30 PT: Postmortem prep and RCA timeline; we will share a draft within 72 hours.

Customer comms: Sean will send a brief note with the above summary and ETA. We apologize for the disruption — our priority is to keep your user flows healthy while we implement a durable fix.

Attachments: canary-metrics-20271011.csv

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
